criterion: Criterion 5. The answer tells the reader that the post-mortem note and the CRM record disagree about when the complaint was raised: it names the disagreement, or calls the note's October date wrong or loosely recalled, or says that no October complaint exists in the system. Answer no in each of these three shapes: the answer never compares the two dates at all; it silently picks one and leaves the reader unaware there was a conflict; or it states both dates, or quotes the note beside the record, WITHOUT telling the reader they are in conflict. A sentence saying the record and the post-mortem disagree about when, such as 'the record disagrees with the post-mortem about when', names the conflict even with no October date in it, wherever it sits and whatever follows it. Once the answer has named the conflict, saying which date to trust, guessing why the note says October, or denying an October event still answers yes. Whether the answer then adopts an October event as its own fact is Criterion 3's question, not this one's. It does not matter which words carry the finding, whether it is split over several sentences, or which language it is in.
